nodes.label: Vite Dev Proxy (API + Socket.IO)
nodes.rationale: API and Socket.IO are proxied from :5173 to :5000 in development (ws:true for the socket upgrade) so the client can use relative URLs everywhere and needs no per-environment base URL.

nodes.label: Lazy Route Code Splitting
nodes.rationale: Heavy screens (recharts analytics, html5-qrcode camera scanner, the whole staff/admin console) are React.lazy imports so the devotee-facing public bundle stays small; light public pages are imported eagerly.

nodes.label: Route Role Sets (CONSOLE_ROLES / ADMIN_ROLES)
nodes.rationale: Console routes are guarded twice — once at the ConsoleLayout wrapper (staff+) and again per admin route (admin+) — so a staff user who reaches an admin URL is redirected rather than shown an empty console.

nodes.label: Provider Composition (Router > Auth > Socket > App)
nodes.rationale: Order is load-bearing: SocketProvider reads the JWT from AuthContext for socket auth and calls useNavigate for notification links, so it must sit inside both BrowserRouter and AuthProvider.

nodes.label: Session Restore with Retry Backoff
nodes.rationale: On boot the stored token is validated via /auth/me. AUTH_INVALID stops immediately (the api interceptor already logs out), but network blips or an API still restarting are retried up to 4 times at 2s so a dev restart does not silently sign the user out.

nodes.label: sd:unauthorized Global Logout Event
nodes.rationale: Decouples the axios layer from React: the interceptor dispatches a window event instead of importing context, so any 401 anywhere collapses the session exactly once.

nodes.label: SocketProvider (Socket.IO lifecycle)
nodes.rationale: autoConnect is false and connect() is deferred by setTimeout(0) so React StrictMode's dev mount/unmount/mount does not open and instantly abort a second connection. The socket is re-created whenever the token changes so auth is re-handshaked.

nodes.label: useSocketEvent subscription hook
nodes.rationale: Handler is kept in a ref so the effect depends only on [socket, event]; the listener is not torn down and re-added every render when callers pass an inline closure.

nodes.label: Reference-Counted Room Membership
nodes.rationale: roomsRef maps 'type:id' to a count of interested components, so two components watching the same temple emit only one subscribe, and unsubscribe fires only when the last one unmounts.

nodes.label: Room Re-Join on Reconnect
nodes.rationale: Server-side rooms are lost when the transport drops, so the connect handler replays every key in roomsRef; without this a reconnected display board would go permanently stale.

nodes.label: Personal Notification Delivery (toast + Web Notification)
nodes.rationale: Server 'notification' pushes render as a clickable toast that navigates to n.link; when document.hidden a system Notification is raised instead so a devotee waiting in queue with the tab backgrounded still sees their call-up.

nodes.label: useFetch data-loading hook
nodes.rationale: reload() keeps the previous data on screen while refetching so periodic refreshes do not flash a loading skeleton.

nodes.label: useInterval (visibility-aware polling)
nodes.rationale: Skips the tick while document.hidden so a backgrounded kiosk or dashboard tab stops hammering the API.

nodes.label: Stale Response Guard (requestId)
nodes.rationale: A monotonic requestId ref discards out-of-order responses so a slow earlier fetch cannot overwrite a newer one.

nodes.label: useLiveTemple (fetch-once then socket-push)
nodes.rationale: Hydrates from GET /temples/:id/live once for first paint, then lets 'live:update' pushes own the state; the templeId equality check filters broadcasts meant for other temples.

nodes.label: ProtectedRoute guard
nodes.rationale: Waits on auth loading before deciding, preserves the attempted path in navigation state for post-login return, and sends a wrong-role user to their own home rather than to /login.

nodes.label: Occupancy Alert Thresholds (90% / 100%)
nodes.rationale: The bar is scaled to 110% of the safe limit so an over-capacity state is still visible rather than pinned at full; 90/100 tick marks make the warning and critical bands readable without relying on colour alone.

nodes.label: LiveLanes (per-lane queue cards)
nodes.rationale: showThroughput reveals whether the people/min rate is measured at the exit gate or merely estimated from capacity, so staff can judge how much to trust the wait estimate.

nodes.label: QrScanner (camera token scanning)
nodes.rationale: A module-level regionCounter gives each instance a unique DOM id so two scanners can coexist; the decoded-text callback goes through a ref so restarting the camera is not needed when the parent's handler changes.

nodes.label: Camera Failure to Guidance Mapping
nodes.rationale: Permission denial, missing device and non-HTTPS origin each map to a specific instruction, and every branch falls back to 'type the token code below' so the gate never blocks on a broken camera.

nodes.label: TempleArt (generated gopuram fallback)
nodes.rationale: Temples without an imageUrl get a drawn gopuram silhouette plus the initial of the name (honorifics like Sri/Arulmigu stripped first), so seeded temples never render a broken or empty image.

nodes.label: Button / LinkButton variant system
nodes.rationale: Variant and size tables are shared by Button and LinkButton through buttonClass so a button and a routed link are visually identical; the xl size exists for the touch-target-sized kiosk controls.

nodes.label: Modal (escape + backdrop dismiss)
nodes.rationale: onMouseDown (not onClick) closes on backdrop, and the panel stops propagation, so a drag that starts inside the dialog and ends on the backdrop does not dismiss it.

nodes.label: Chart-to-Table Accessibility Toggle
nodes.rationale: Every charted value must also be readable without colour or hover, so ChartFrame renders the same rows as a sortable-column table behind a toggle instead of relying on tooltips.

nodes.label: Devotee vs Admin Forecast Modes (showActual)
nodes.rationale: One component serves two audiences: devotees see bars coloured by crowd level with 'good time to visit' hints, admins see actual entries as bars against the model's prediction as a line on a shared axis to eyeball model error.

nodes.label: DailyTrendChart
nodes.rationale: Festival days are recoloured per-Cell and given their own legend entry so the spikes the forecast model keys on are visually attributable.

nodes.label: WeekHeatmap (weekday x hour)
nodes.rationale: Built as a CSS grid rather than a charting primitive, on a single-hue ramp, with the week ordered Mon-Sun; every cell is also emitted as a table row for the ChartFrame table view.

nodes.label: FeatureImportance (Random Forest inputs)
nodes.rationale: Renders the ML service's feature importances as a labelled, value-annotated bar list with human names for cyclic encodings (hour_sin/hour_cos), making the model explainable to non-technical temple admins.

nodes.label: NAV Section Config (role + temple gating)
nodes.rationale: Sections declare roles and needsTemple; items that need a temple scope render as disabled text rather than disappearing, so a superadmin who has not picked a temple can still see what the console offers.

nodes.label: Superadmin Temple Scope Switch
nodes.rationale: The selected temple id is persisted under TEMPLE_SCOPE_KEY and sent by the api layer so every /admin and /staff request is scoped server-side; the Outlet is keyed by scope so switching temples remounts all child pages instead of showing another temple's stale state.

nodes.label: Unread Crowd Alert Badge
nodes.rationale: Seeded from GET /admin/alerts then incremented live by the 'alert:new' room event, so an admin on any console page sees a capacity alert without polling.

nodes.label: Console Outlet Context {temple, reloadTemple, clearAlerts}
nodes.rationale: The resolved temple is fetched once by the shell and handed down through router context so each console page does not refetch /staff/context.

nodes.label: Public Footer (SMS / kiosk fallback)
nodes.rationale: Advertises the no-smartphone paths (kiosk walk-in token, SMS 'STATUS <code>') in the footer of every public page, since digital-exclusion coverage is a core requirement of the project.

nodes.label: Guarded localStorage Wrapper
nodes.rationale: Every localStorage access is wrapped in try/catch because it throws in private mode or when site data is blocked; reads degrade to null and writes are silently dropped rather than crashing the app shell.

nodes.label: Axios API Client
nodes.rationale: baseURL is built from VITE_API_URL with an empty-string fallback so the same build works behind a dev proxy (same-origin /api) and against a separate deployed API host.

nodes.label: Session Expiry Response Interceptor
nodes.rationale: Logout is triggered only by error code AUTH_INVALID while a token is actually stored, so an ordinary wrong-password 401 on the login form does not evict an unrelated session.

nodes.label: sd:unauthorized Window Event
nodes.rationale: A DOM event decouples the axios layer from React state: the interceptor cannot call a hook, so it broadcasts and the auth context listens.

nodes.label: errorMessage Helper
nodes.rationale: Prefers the server's structured error.message, then special-cases ERR_NETWORK and 502/503/504 into an actionable 'Is the API running?' hint, so every page can surface one consistent failure string.

nodes.label: X-Temple-Id Scope Header
nodes.rationale: Superadmin temple impersonation is carried as a header rather than in every URL; the server ignores it for non-superadmins, so it is safe to send unconditionally.

nodes.label: CHART_COLORS Palette
nodes.rationale: Colours were checked against a data-viz palette validator for a CVD-safe actual/predicted pair at >= 3:1 on white; crowd levels reuse the reserved status colours and are always paired with a text label so colour is never the sole channel.

nodes.label: homePathFor Role Landing Router
nodes.rationale: Post-login destination is derived from role in one place so staff land on the scanner, admins on the console and devotees on the public list, instead of each auth page hardcoding redirects.

nodes.label: Asia/Kolkata Default Timezone
nodes.rationale: Every formatter takes an explicit timeZone argument defaulting to Asia/Kolkata, so per-temple timezones override the default without the browser's local zone ever leaking into displayed queue times.

nodes.label: fmtDateStr Calendar-Date Formatter
nodes.rationale: 'YYYY-MM-DD' values are calendar dates, not instants, so this parses them at UTC midnight and formats in UTC to avoid the off-by-one-day shift that temple-timezone formatting would introduce.

nodes.label: todayIn Temple-Local Today
nodes.rationale: Uses the en-CA locale because it renders ISO-shaped YYYY-MM-DD, giving a date key that matches the server's slot/festival date strings.

nodes.label: rupees Currency Formatter
nodes.rationale: A zero price renders as 'Free' rather than Rs.0, because free darshan is the common case and the wording matters more than the number.

nodes.label: Gate Scanner Confirmation Beep
nodes.rationale: Success and failure use distinct tone pairs and waveforms (rising sine vs falling square) plus a vibration pattern, so gate staff can confirm a scan without looking at the screen; the whole routine is try/catch'd and the AudioContext lazily created because audio is unavailable or blocked on many kiosk devices.

nodes.label: Retrain Model Action
nodes.rationale: The Retrain button is disabled unless the Python service reports online, and success reloads both the model card and the week forecast because retraining invalidates the cached predictions.

nodes.label: ML Model Metrics Panel
nodes.rationale: Reports R2, MAE and sample count alongside a weekday-hour baseline MAE and improvement percentage, so the Random Forest is justified against the naive average rather than presented on its own.

nodes.label: Optimistic Active Toggle
nodes.rationale: The list is mutated locally before the PATCH so the switch feels instant on a slow temple connection; a failure toasts the error and reloads to resync rather than trying to roll back by hand.

nodes.label: Pause/Resume Entry Control
nodes.rationale: Pausing is gated behind a confirmation modal that collects a devotee-facing reason, because the action refuses scans at every gate and the reason is what devotees see on their phones and on the entrance board.

nodes.label: Throttled Live Stats Refresh
nodes.rationale: Socket live:update events are throttled to one stats reload per 15s and backed by a 60s interval, so a burst of gate scans cannot storm the stats endpoint while the panel still recovers if a socket message is missed.

nodes.label: Save Temple Section Action
nodes.rationale: One save() handles profile, rules and festivals against the same PATCH /admin/temple endpoint, keyed by a section string so each form can show its own loading state without duplicating error handling.

nodes.label: Slot Sync Result Message
nodes.rationale: Any settings change can silently regenerate future slots, so the created/updated/removed counts returned by the server are appended to the success toast to make that side effect visible.

nodes.label: SETTING_FIELDS Crowd & Booking Rules
nodes.rationale: The numeric rule set is declared as data rather than markup so the whole form is one map, and it centralises the knobs (safe limit, booking window, check-in grace, walk-in release, festival multiplier) that every other surface reads back from temple.settings.

nodes.label: Festival Calendar Editor
nodes.rationale: Add and remove both rewrite the entire festivals array through the same PATCH, keeping the server contract a single replace instead of per-item endpoints; only future-dated festivals are listed.

nodes.label: Darshan Type Editor
nodes.rationale: Each darshan type owns its slot length, per-slot capacity, walk-in share and priority flag, because a type is also a physical queue lane at the gate.

nodes.label: Manual Slot Sync Action
nodes.rationale: Slots are normally generated automatically for the booking window; the manual sync exists as an escape hatch when timings or types were changed out of band, and reports the same created/updated/removed counts.

nodes.label: Create Staff Account Action
nodes.rationale: Creation errors render inside the modal via a form-level banner instead of a toast, so the admin can correct the field without the message disappearing behind the dialog.

nodes.label: Update Staff Member Action
nodes.rationale: One PATCH serves both the active toggle and the admin password reset; the toggle is disabled on the admin's own row so nobody can lock themselves out of the console.

nodes.label: Login Page
nodes.rationale: Redirect target is location.state.from when a guard bounced the user here, otherwise the role's home path, so a deep link survives an interstitial login.

nodes.label: Demo Account Quick-Fill
nodes.rationale: Seed-script credentials for all four roles are exposed as click-to-fill buttons for reviewer demos, guarded by import.meta.env.DEV so the panel is stripped from production builds.

nodes.label: Register Page
nodes.rationale: Password confirmation is checked client-side and the confirm field is stripped from the payload before submit; phone is optional and labelled as the channel for SMS confirmations and slot reminders.

nodes.label: Confirm Booking Action
nodes.rationale: A failed booking reloads the slot list, because the most likely cause is that the seats were taken between render and submit; on success the ticket replaces the form rather than navigating away.

nodes.label: localHourOf Slot Hour Helper
nodes.rationale: Converts a slot's absolute start time to the temple-local hour so it can be matched against the hour-keyed forecast map.

nodes.label: Live Slot Seat Subscription
nodes.rationale: The page joins the temple socket room and patches single slots in place on slot:update, so seats-left counts stay honest while the devotee deliberates without refetching the grid.

nodes.label: Crowd-Aware Slot Picker
nodes.rationale: Each slot button carries its forecast crowd level and a sparkle marker for recommended hours, steering demand toward quieter times at the point of choice rather than in a separate chart.

nodes.label: Ten-Minute Booking Cutoff
nodes.rationale: Slots ending within ten minutes are shown as Closed so devotees cannot book a slot they could never reach the gate for; the ten minutes is a client-side literal, not a temple setting.

nodes.label: Self-Service Password Change
nodes.rationale: Requires the current password and posts to a dedicated endpoint rather than PATCHing the user record, keeping credential changes separate from profile edits.

nodes.label: Entrance Display Board
nodes.rationale: A full-screen dark board for TVs at the entrance, aimed at devotees without smartphones; large type, a live clock and a connection dot make it readable and trustworthy from across the courtyard.

nodes.label: Unattended Reload Loop
nodes.rationale: Boards run unattended with nobody to press refresh, so a failed first load retries every 10s and the forecast refreshes every 15 minutes; the error state itself says 'Retrying...' instead of dead-ending.

nodes.label: Temple QR Handoff
nodes.rationale: The board prints a QR to its own temple page plus an SMS STATUS fallback, giving a path onto the phone for devotees with a smartphone and a path without one for everyone else.

nodes.label: Wait-Time Colour Thresholds
nodes.rationale: Local 20/45-minute thresholds pick bright red/amber/emerald tuned for a dark board at distance, instead of reusing the light-background crowd-level tokens.

nodes.label: How It Works Steps
nodes.rationale: Four steps narrate the whole product as one story: book a slot, show the QR at the gate, track the live queue, plan with the ML forecast.

nodes.label: Token Code Lookup
nodes.rationale: A logged-out devotee can reach live queue status by typing the printed token code, which is upper-cased before navigating to the tracking route.

nodes.label: Client-Side Temple Search
nodes.rationale: Filtering by name, deity, city or state is memoised in the browser over the already-fetched list, which stays cheap at the project's temple count and keeps typing instant; the list itself re-polls every 30s so wait times stay current.

nodes.label: Temple Detail Page
nodes.rationale: Booking is offered only to anonymous visitors and devotee-role users, so staff and admins browsing the public page are not invited into the devotee flow.

nodes.label: Self-Service Token Kiosk
nodes.rationale: The device itself is logged in with a staff account while devotees only tap through welcome -> type -> people -> done, so walk-ins need no registration; every control is oversized for touch and name/phone stay optional.

nodes.label: Issue Walk-in Token Action
nodes.rationale: Falls back to the name 'Walk-in Devotee' when the field is left blank, so the slip is always printable without forcing an anonymous devotee to type.

nodes.label: Idle Kiosk Reset
nodes.rationale: A 45-second timer, re-armed on every interaction, returns the shared kiosk to the welcome screen so one devotee's half-finished flow and personal details never greet the next person.

nodes.label: Printed Token Slip
nodes.rationale: Chrome print is driven straight from the page with no-print classes hiding the kiosk chrome, so a paper slip is the takeaway for devotees with no phone.

nodes.label: QR Gate Scanner Page
nodes.rationale: Single screen doubles as entry and exit gate via a mode toggle so one device/operator can serve either gate; switching mode clears the last-scan memo so the same token can be re-scanned for the opposite action.

nodes.label: Scan Handler (duplicate-scan guard)
nodes.rationale: A camera QR scanner re-fires continuously on the same code; a 4s code+timestamp window plus a busy flag prevents double entry/exit posts to /staff/scan. Manual form submit deliberately resets the memo so a staff member can force a repeat.

nodes.label: Scan Result Panel
nodes.rationale: Large full-colour pass/fail panel with aria-live=assertive, sized for a gate operator glancing at a device in crowd conditions; paired with an audio beep for eyes-free confirmation.

nodes.label: Walk-in Counter Page
nodes.rationale: Counter-clerk flow: slot defaults to 'next available' and name defaults to 'Walk-in Devotee' so a token can be issued with only a group size, keeping the physical counter queue moving.

nodes.label: Temple Scope Switch (manage)
nodes.rationale: Writes the chosen temple id to persisted TEMPLE_SCOPE_KEY then does a full window.location.assign instead of a client-side route change, so every cached console view and socket subscription is rebuilt under the new scope.

nodes.label: Smart Darshan ML Flask Service
nodes.rationale: Bound to 127.0.0.1 and documented as called by the Node API rather than the browser: the Python service is an internal, unauthenticated sidecar and the Express API is the only trust boundary.

nodes.label: ML JSON Error Handlers
nodes.rationale: Every failure is converted to a JSON {error} body so the Node client sees one uniform error shape; unexpected exceptions are logged but reported generically to avoid leaking internals across the service boundary.

nodes.label: ModelStore (per-temple model registry)
nodes.rationale: One joblib file per temple keyed by a strict 24-hex ObjectId pattern (path-traversal guard), with an mtime-keyed in-process cache and a lock so concurrent predict requests do not reload or race a retrain.

nodes.label: ModelStore.train
nodes.rationale: Holds out 20% to report honest MAE/R2, then refits on the full dataset before saving, so metrics are unbiased while the shipped model uses all history. Requires >= 50 records rather than training a meaningless model on a new temple.

nodes.label: ModelStore.predict
nodes.rationale: Reindexes incoming features by the feature list stored inside the saved bundle rather than the current module constant, so an older saved model keeps working after FEATURES changes; negative predictions are clamped to 0 because footfall cannot be negative.

nodes.label: build_features (feature engineering)
nodes.rationale: Adds is_weekend and sin/cos cyclical encodings of the hour so hour 23 and hour 0 are neighbours in feature space instead of maximally distant integers; missing-field check raises a 400-level ModelError rather than a pandas KeyError.

nodes.label: Seasonal Baseline MAE
nodes.rationale: Computes the error of a naive 'average for this weekday/hour/festival' guess and reports improvementPct, so the project can demonstrate the Random Forest actually beats a trivial heuristic rather than quoting R2 alone.

nodes.label: Random Forest Footfall Regressor
nodes.rationale: RandomForestRegressor (200 trees, max_depth 14, min_samples_leaf 2, fixed random_state) chosen for small tabular temple histories: handles non-linear hour/festival interactions without scaling, resists overfitting on sparse data, and exposes feature_importances_ for explaining crowd drivers to temple admins.

nodes.label: createApp (Express app factory)
nodes.rationale: App construction is a factory separate from server.js so the app can be built without binding a port or opening sockets; trust proxy 1 is set for correct client IPs behind a reverse proxy, and request logging is skipped for /api/health to keep dev logs readable.

nodes.label: API Bootstrap (server.js main)
nodes.rationale: Ordered startup: DB first, optional demo seed only when the temple collection is empty, then HTTP + socket, then cron jobs; SIGINT/SIGTERM close the server and disconnect Mongo so a dev restart does not leak connections.

nodes.label: connectDB (retrying Mongo connect)
nodes.rationale: Retries for up to 40 x 3s because `npm run dev` starts the API and MongoDB together and the API would otherwise crash-loop; the connection string is redacted before logging so credentials never reach the console.

nodes.label: Environment Configuration
nodes.rationale: Every setting has a working localhost default so the project runs with no .env for a demo; derived flags (smsEnabled, isProduction, publicClientUrl) are computed once, and booting production with the dev JWT secret throws at startup rather than shipping a guessable secret.

nodes.label: userFromJwt (token to live user)
nodes.rationale: Only jwt.verify failures return null; the User lookup is deliberately not wrapped in try/catch so a transient database outage surfaces as a 500 instead of a fake 401 that would log every user out. Role is re-read from the database each request, so deactivating a user takes effect before the JWT expires.

nodes.label: optionalAuth middleware
nodes.rationale: Public temple/browse routes need to know the viewer when signed in but must never reject anonymous devotees, so a bad token silently yields no req.user.

nodes.label: Central Error Handler
nodes.rationale: Translates Mongoose CastError/ValidationError/E11000 and body-parser failures into stable {error:{message,code}} envelopes so the React client can branch on machine codes; stack traces are attached only for non-production 5xx, and only genuinely unexpected errors are console-logged.

nodes.label: templeScope middleware
nodes.rationale: Multi-tenant isolation: staff/admin temple id is taken from the authenticated user and never from the URL, so no path parameter can be tampered with to reach another temple; only superadmins may name a temple, via the X-Temple-Id header, and they alone may open an inactive temple.

nodes.label: updateTemple (profile & settings)
nodes.rationale: Any change to opening hours, festivals or settings invalidates derived state, so the handler re-runs slot generation, clears the forecast cache and republishes the live snapshot in one transaction-like sequence rather than leaving stale slots behind.

nodes.label: updateControls (entry pause)
nodes.rationale: Crowd-safety kill switch: publishes with a zero debounce (schedulePublish(id, 0)) because a pause must reach gate devices and devotee screens immediately, unlike routine snapshot updates.

nodes.label: listSlots with per-status head counts
nodes.rationale: Uses a Token aggregation grouped by slot+status summing groupSize so counts are people rather than tokens, and runs it in parallel with the slot query.

nodes.label: createStaff (provision staff account)
nodes.rationale: Admins may only create accounts inside their own temple scope, and updateStaff blocks self-deactivation so a temple cannot lock out its last admin.

nodes.label: register (devotee signup)
nodes.rationale: Self-service signup always forces role 'devotee'; privileged roles can only be created through the admin or superadmin paths.

nodes.label: login
nodes.rationale: Wrong email and wrong password return one identical BAD_CREDENTIALS message to avoid account enumeration, while a deactivated account gets a distinct ACCOUNT_DISABLED code the client can explain.

nodes.label: Inbound SMS Webhook
nodes.rationale: Feature-phone channel so devotees without smartphones or data can still get queue status; a bare token code anywhere in the message short-circuits command parsing, and anything unrecognised returns help text instead of an error.

nodes.label: Token Status SMS Text
nodes.rationale: Per-status phrasing (queue position for checked_in, slot window and entry-opens time for booked) keeps each reply inside a single SMS while answering the one question that status implies.

nodes.label: Temple Wait SMS Text
nodes.rationale: Matches the free-text argument against slug, name or city with an escaped regex so devotees can text an approximate temple name.

nodes.label: TwiML Reply Writer
nodes.rationale: Hand-builds the TwiML XML with explicit entity escaping rather than pulling in a template engine, since temple names and devotee text flow straight into the XML body.

nodes.label: context (gate device bootstrap)
nodes.rationale: One call returns public temple profile plus controls plus the live snapshot so a counter or gate device can cold-start with a single request.

nodes.label: walkinSlots (counter slot list)
nodes.rationale: Filters to slots ending more than 5 minutes out, so the counter never offers a slot that will close before the devotee reaches the gate.

nodes.label: listTokens (search & queue list)
nodes.rationale: A text search spans all dates while an empty search is pinned to today, so staff looking up a specific code can find an old token but the default view stays scoped to the current day; the 'enterable' filter encodes the check-in early/late grace window from temple settings.

nodes.label: Superadmin listTemples
nodes.rationale: Live snapshots are fetched with a 30s staleness allowance and .catch(() => null) per temple so one unhealthy temple cannot fail the whole platform table.

nodes.label: createTemple (onboarding)
nodes.rationale: Creates temple, its first admin user and its initial slots in one call; since Mongo has no transaction here, a failed admin save deletes the just-created temple to avoid an orphan tenant with no way in.

nodes.label: DEFAULT_DARSHAN_TYPES
nodes.rationale: Seeds every new temple with free Sarva Darshan, paid Special Entry and a priority lane for seniors/differently-abled, each with its own slot length, capacity and walk-in reservation percentage, so a temple is usable immediately and the walk-in vs online split is a per-darshan-type policy from day one.

nodes.label: findActiveTemple (id or slug)
nodes.rationale: Public routes accept either an ObjectId or a human-readable slug so temple URLs are shareable, and the isActive filter is baked in so a deactivated temple 404s on every public endpoint.

nodes.label: Public getSlots (booking window)
nodes.rationale: Rejects dates outside [today, today + bookingWindowDays - 1] with a DATE_OUT_OF_RANGE code so the client can show the allowed range instead of an empty slot list.

nodes.label: startJobs (cron scheduler)
nodes.rationale: Staggered schedule keeps the minute boundary free: tokens every minute, slot sync at :05, untrained-model catch-up at :20, full retrain at 02:30 off-peak, live snapshots on a 30s setInterval. An immediate slot sync and a 5s-delayed initial training run mean a fresh clone is usable without waiting for the first cron tick.

nodes.label: safely (re-entrancy wrapper)
nodes.rationale: Each cron task carries a running flag and swallows errors into a named log line, so a slow pass cannot overlap itself and one failing job can never crash the API process.

nodes.label: tokenMaintenance job
nodes.rationale: Single minute-by-minute pass does three lifecycle transitions per temple - expire missed bookings past the late grace window, auto-complete stale check-ins (recording the exit footfall so occupancy self-heals when staff forget to scan out), and send pre-slot reminders guarded by reminderSentAt so a reminder is never sent twice. Snapshot republish happens once per temple only if something changed.

nodes.label: trainModels job
nodes.rationale: Health-checks the Python service first and returns quietly when it is offline, because the forecast path degrades to historical averages; per-temple training failures are logged and skipped so one temple with too little history does not stop the rest.

nodes.label: validate() zod request middleware
nodes.rationale: Parsed values are written to req.valid instead of overwriting req.params/query/body because Express 5 makes req.query read-only; the first zod issue is flattened into a human-readable message while the full issue list is carried as AppError details with code VALIDATION_ERROR.

nodes.label: Alert model (crowd alerts)
nodes.rationale: Machine-raised crowd alerts are persisted per temple with an acknowledged flag and a (templeId, createdAt desc) index so admin dashboards can page the newest alerts cheaply.

nodes.label: Announcement model (admin notices)
nodes.rationale: Human-authored notices keep an isActive flag rather than being deleted, so the (templeId, isActive, createdAt desc) index serves the public 'current notices' query directly.

nodes.label: FootfallLog model (hourly entries/exits)
nodes.rationale: One row per temple/date/hour with a unique compound index, so footfall recording is an idempotent upsert and the table doubles as the labelled training history for the prediction model. dayOfWeek and isFestival are denormalised onto the row so the model can read features without re-joining Temple.

nodes.label: Slot model (darshan time slots)
nodes.rationale: Capacities and booked counters count people, not tokens (a family of four consumes four seats). Online and walk-in capacity are tracked as separate counters on the same slot so the walk-in reserve cannot be eaten by online bookings.

nodes.label: Temple model
nodes.rationale: The temple document is the multi-tenant root: operating hours, per-tenant policy (settings), live operational state (controls), festival calendar and trained-model metadata all hang off it, so a single fetch gives any request everything it needs to reason about one temple.

nodes.label: DarshanType embedded subdocument
nodes.rationale: Darshan lanes are embedded in Temple rather than a separate collection because they are always read with the temple; walkinPercent holds back a share of every slot for walk-in devotees and isPriority marks the senior-citizen / differently-abled lane.

nodes.label: Temple settings (operational policy)
nodes.rationale: Every operational knob is per-temple data rather than a constant: unbooked online seats release to walk-ins walkinReleaseMin before a slot, devotees never scanned out are auto-completed after autoCompleteAfterMin, festivals multiply capacity by festivalCapacityMultiplier, and autoPauseAtCapacity opts a temple into automatic entry pausing.

nodes.label: Temple controls (entry pause state)
nodes.rationale: Live gate state (entryPaused, pauseReason, pausedAt) lives on the temple document so both the admin dashboard and the automatic capacity guard write to one authoritative place.

nodes.label: Temple mlModel metrics block
nodes.rationale: Each temple stores its own trained-model metadata (algorithm, MAE, r2, feature importances) plus baselineMae — the error of a naive 'average for this weekday and hour' guess — so improvementPct can justify the ML model against a trivial baseline.

nodes.label: Temple.toPublicJSON() projection
nodes.rationale: An explicit allow-list projection: inactive darshan types, walkinPercent, maxOccupancy, controls and mlModel are withheld from visitors, exposing only the booking-relevant subset of settings.

nodes.label: User model
nodes.rationale: passwordHash is select:false and additionally stripped in the toJSON transform, so the hash cannot leak through an accidental serialisation even if a query explicitly selects it. Staff and temple admins carry exactly one templeId, which is what makes tenant scoping possible.

nodes.label: ROLES (devotee/staff/admin/superadmin)
nodes.rationale: A four-tier ladder where each tier is a superset of the one below; routers express access by listing the tiers allowed rather than by per-permission checks.

nodes.label: Admin router (/api/admin)
nodes.rationale: authenticate + requireRole('admin','superadmin') + templeScope are applied once with router.use so every admin endpoint is tenant-scoped by construction and no individual route can forget the check.

nodes.label: Admin settings zod schema
nodes.rationale: Declared .partial() so PATCH can send any subset of settings; bounds are re-stated here rather than inherited from mongoose so bad input is rejected at the edge with a field-level message.

nodes.label: darshanTypeFields zod shape
nodes.rationale: One field map reused strictly for POST and .partial() for PATCH, so create and update can never drift apart.

nodes.label: authLimiter rate limit (50 / 15 min)
nodes.rationale: Applied only to register and login (the credential-guessing surface), not to the authenticated /me endpoints; returns the same { error: { message, code } } envelope the rest of the API uses so the client needs no special case.

nodes.label: POST /api/auth/login
nodes.rationale: Login validates password only as a non-empty string rather than with the strong `password` schema, so tightening the password policy never locks out existing accounts.

nodes.label: API root router (/api)
nodes.rationale: One mount table maps URL prefixes to role-tiered routers; the Twilio inbound SMS webhook is mounted with its own urlencoded body parser because it is form-encoded rather than JSON.

nodes.label: GET /api/health
nodes.rationale: Reports the three external dependencies separately (mongo readyState, ML service reachability, Twilio vs mock SMS) so a degraded demo can be diagnosed from one call.

nodes.label: Shared zod field validators
nodes.rationale: Field-level validators (email, password, personName, phone, groupSize...) are centralised so every router enforces the same rules and the same user-facing error text; email is normalised (trim + lowercase) at the edge to match the lowercase unique index on User.email.

nodes.label: dateStr validator (YYYY-MM-DD)
nodes.rationale: Dates travel as temple-local YYYY-MM-DD strings rather than Date objects, so a request never carries a timezone the server has to guess at.

nodes.label: objectId validator
nodes.rationale: Malformed ids are rejected as a 400 validation error at the edge instead of surfacing as a mongoose CastError deeper in a controller.

nodes.label: POST /api/staff/walkin
nodes.rationale: slotId is optional so a gate operator can issue a token for a lane and let the server pick the current walk-in slot.

nodes.label: POST /api/staff/scan (entry/exit)
nodes.rationale: A single endpoint handles both directions with an action discriminator, so one scanner UI drives entry and exit.

nodes.label: GET /api/staff/tokens
nodes.rationale: The `enterable` query flag arrives as the strings 'true'/'false' and is transformed to a boolean in the schema, because query strings have no boolean type.

nodes.label: GET /api/staff/context
nodes.rationale: Returns temple + live snapshot in one call so a gate terminal can boot with a single request.

nodes.label: Superadmin router (/api/superadmin)
nodes.rationale: The only router without templeScope, because platform-level operations deliberately cross tenants; temple creation takes the first admin's credentials in the same payload so a tenant is never left without an operator. Temples are deactivated via isActive rather than deleted.

nodes.label: Public temple router (/api/temples)
nodes.rationale: The only unauthenticated router: discovery, slots, live status, forecast and announcements are public, and routes accept :idOrSlug so temples have shareable human-readable URLs.

nodes.label: localDb script (in-process MongoDB)
nodes.rationale: Runs mongodb-memory-server on the standard port with a persistent dbPath so a reviewer needs no MongoDB install yet keeps data between runs; it probes the port first and exits cleanly if something is already listening, and stops with doCleanup:false so the data folder survives.

nodes.label: seed script (npm run seed)
nodes.rationale: Refuses to seed over an existing database unless --reset is passed, and offers --24h to force temples open around the clock so late-night testing still has live slots.

nodes.label: seedDatabase()
nodes.rationale: Demo state is built by driving the real booking, slot and footfall services rather than inserting documents directly, so seeded data obeys the same capacity and counter invariants as production traffic; bookings are made with { silent: true } to suppress SMS during seeding.

nodes.label: generateFootfall() synthetic history
nodes.rationale: Synthesises 90 days of hourly counts from an explicit generative model — hourly profile x weekday factor x sinusoidal seasonality x festival multiplier x popularity, clipped to capacity and jittered — precisely so the ML model has learnable structure to recover. Today is only filled up to the current hour so 'now' looks live rather than pre-ordained.

nodes.label: mulberry32 deterministic PRNG
nodes.rationale: A seeded PRNG replaces Math.random so every seed run produces byte-identical demo data, making screenshots, metrics and demos reproducible.

nodes.label: buildFestivals()
nodes.rationale: Festivals are placed relative to today (recurring Ekadashi every 15 days plus a three-day major festival in the past) so the generated history always contains festival examples for the model and upcoming ones for the UI, whenever the demo is run.

nodes.label: TEMPLES demo tenant definitions
nodes.rationale: Three temples in different cities, each with a free lane, a paid lane and a priority lane and a different popularity/occupancy, so multi-tenancy, lane pricing and the walk-in reserve are all visible in a demo.

nodes.label: DEMO_PASSWORDS credential set
nodes.rationale: Fixed per-role passwords printed as a console.table at the end of seeding so a reviewer can log in as each role immediately; explicitly marked local-development-only.

nodes.label: HOUR_PROFILE / DAY_FACTOR crowd shape
nodes.rationale: Encodes domain knowledge as data: twin morning and evening peaks with a midday lull, and heavier Sunday/Friday-Saturday weekday factors, which is the signal the trained model is expected to rediscover.

nodes.label: Crowd simulator script
nodes.rationale: Drives the live demo through the real HTTP API with a real staff login rather than writing to the database, so sockets, wait-time maths, alerts and display boards all exercise the production path; --surge skews the action mix towards arrivals to force queue growth and trip the capacity alert.

nodes.label: simulator main loop
nodes.rationale: Picks an action by weighted random draw each tick and falls back (chosen action -> scanEntry -> issueWalkin) when an action has nothing to do, so the simulation never stalls on an empty queue; a second interval prints per-lane queue and wait figures every 15s.

nodes.label: simulator api() fetch helper
nodes.rationale: Holds the JWT in a module-level variable and unwraps the API's { error: { message } } envelope into a thrown Error, so callers can use plain try/catch.

nodes.label: simulator scanExit()
nodes.rationale: Only exits devotees who have been checked in for over a minute, so simulated visits have a plausible non-zero dwell time and wait-time estimates stay sane.

nodes.label: simulator weightedLane()
nodes.rationale: Chooses a darshan lane in proportion to its throughput (capacityPerSlot / slotMinutes) so simulated arrivals distribute across lanes the way real demand would, instead of uniformly.

nodes.label: raiseAlert()
nodes.rationale: Persists the alert and pushes it to the admin:<templeId> socket room in one step, so a dashboard that was open and one opened later both see the same alert.

nodes.label: checkOccupancy() capacity guard
nodes.rationale: Fires only on escalation (severity strictly greater than the last level seen for that temple) so admins are not spammed while the queue hovers at a threshold; thresholds are 90% warning and 100% critical of safe occupancy. At critical it optionally auto-pauses entry, but only when the temple opted in via autoPauseAtCapacity and entry is not already paused, then dynamically imports liveStats to republish the snapshot — a deferred import that avoids a circular dependency between the alert and live-stats services.

nodes.label: lastLevels in-memory escalation state
nodes.rationale: Per-temple last severity is kept in a process-local Map rather than the database: cheap and adequate for a single-process deployment, but it resets on restart and would mis-deduplicate across multiple server instances.

nodes.label: reserveSeats (atomic seat reservation)
nodes.rationale: Capacity check and increment happen in one findOneAndUpdate with an $expr guard, so two devotees racing for the last seats can never overbook; separate online/walkin counters are both bounded by a combined-total condition.

nodes.label: createTokenDoc (unique code retry)
nodes.rationale: Retries up to 5 times on E11000 duplicate-key collisions of the random code rather than pre-checking uniqueness, so no lock or extra read is needed; any other error is rethrown untouched.

nodes.label: cancelToken
nodes.rationale: Status-conditional findOneAndUpdate makes double cancellation impossible; temple managers may cancel after the slot has started, owners may not.

nodes.label: tokenData (token document builder)
nodes.rationale: Pre-stamps reminderSentAt when the slot already starts inside the reminder window, so the reminder job skips tokens for which a reminder would be pointless.

nodes.label: getForecast (hourly crowd forecast)
nodes.rationale: Prefers the trained scikit-learn model but degrades to historical averages when the Python service is down, and labels the result with its source so the UI can be honest about prediction quality.

nodes.label: historicalAverage fallback predictor
nodes.rationale: Three-level backoff: exact weekday+hour+festival average, then the same weekday's non-festival average scaled 1.8x for festivals, then the hour's overall mean, so a forecast is always produced even with sparse history.

nodes.label: trainTempleModel
nodes.rationale: Refuses to train below 100 hourly records and only uses days strictly before today, so a partially-recorded current day cannot skew the model; metrics are persisted on the Temple document for admin visibility.

nodes.label: retrainInBackground
nodes.rationale: A 404 from the predictor means the service is running but has no model file (e.g. a fresh clone); training is fired off asynchronously behind a 10-minute per-temple lockout so user requests never wait on it and it cannot thrash.

nodes.label: Forecast TTL cache
nodes.rationale: 10-minute TTL keyed by templeId:date; forecasts change slowly, so caching absorbs repeated dashboard polls and keeps the Python round-trip off the hot path.

nodes.label: Wait-time engine
nodes.rationale: Wait is modelled per lane as inQueue / throughput, where inQueue comes from entry scans not yet matched by exit scans and throughput from recent exits; this makes wait time an observed quantity rather than a configured guess.

nodes.label: computeSnapshot
nodes.rationale: Measured throughput requires 10+ exited people and is divided by the span actually observed (floor 5 min, cap 15 min) so a gate that only began exiting people recently is not read as slow; auto-completed tokens are excluded because they were never really processed.

nodes.label: tokenQueueInfo (per-token queue position)
nodes.rationale: Position is derived by counting people checked in earlier in the same lane, so it stays correct without maintaining any explicit queue ordering.

nodes.label: In-memory snapshot store
nodes.rationale: A 10-second freshness window serves live reads from process memory instead of re-running four Mongo aggregations per request; staleness of a few seconds is acceptable for a crowd display.

nodes.label: ML service HTTP wrapper
nodes.rationale: One fetch wrapper with per-operation AbortSignal timeouts (2s health, 8s predict, 120s train) so a hung Python service cannot stall Express; non-2xx responses are rethrown as Errors carrying .status, which is what lets callers branch on 404 (model missing).

nodes.label: notifyTokenHolder (dual-channel notify)
nodes.rationale: One entry point fans a message out to the in-app socket and optionally SMS; the SMS call is deliberately not awaited so booking and scan responses stay fast even if Twilio is slow.

nodes.label: scanToken (entry/exit gate scan)
nodes.rationale: The gate scan is the single source of truth for queue state: entry adds people, exit removes them. Status transitions use conditional updates so a double scan loses the race instead of corrupting counts, and every rejection carries a machine-readable code plus the serialized token so the scanner UI can show who was rejected and why.

nodes.label: defaultThroughput (designed lane rate)
nodes.rationale: Designed capacity per minute is the safe fallback when too few exits have been observed to measure a real rate.

nodes.label: buildSlotsForDate
nodes.rationale: Builds slots in memory without saving, so the same generator can be used for both preview and reconciliation; walk-in capacity is carved out of total capacity by percentage.

nodes.label: slotAvailability (seats left)
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the reservation rule on the read side: quota-limited normally, whole remaining pool for walk-ins once the release window opens.

nodes.label: sendSms (Twilio, fail-soft)
nodes.rationale: Never throws and logs to console when Twilio credentials are absent, so SMS outages or a developer machine cannot break bookings and scans; the Twilio SDK is imported lazily so the dependency is only loaded when actually used.

nodes.label: isValidTwilioRequest (webhook signature)
nodes.rationale: Signature verification is skipped when no authToken/webhookUrl is configured, so local development and the API test suite can post to the inbound endpoint unsigned.

nodes.label: todayStats (actual vs predicted)
nodes.rationale: Joins the forecast's hourly predictions with the same day's recorded footfall so admins see model accuracy in situ rather than as a separate metric.

nodes.label: trendStats (daily totals + heatmap)
nodes.rationale: Aggregates in JS over lean logs rather than in Mongo, and excludes today so partial data never distorts the weekday/weekend/festival averages.

nodes.label: initSocket (Socket.IO bootstrap)
nodes.rationale: JWT on the handshake is optional: anonymous sockets still connect so public temple and token rooms work without login, while identity is only needed for personal and admin rooms. The snapshot provider is injected rather than imported, avoiding a socket<->liveStats import cycle.

nodes.label: roomFor (room authorization)
nodes.rationale: Client-supplied room ids are validated, never trusted: temple/admin ids must be ObjectIds, token rooms must match the code regex, and admin rooms require superadmin or a role whose templeId matches.

nodes.label: Socket room namespace scheme
nodes.rationale: Four room prefixes (temple:, token:, user:, admin:) split public broadcast from personal and privileged traffic; the token code itself acts as the shared secret for its public status room.

nodes.label: AppError (client-safe HTTP error)
nodes.rationale: Carries status, a machine code and optional details so the error handler can distinguish errors safe to show the client from unexpected ones.

nodes.label: generateTokenCode
nodes.rationale: Alphabet omits 0/O and 1/I/L so codes stay unambiguous when read aloud at a counter or typed from a printed slip; crypto.randomInt is used rather than Math.random so codes are not guessable.

nodes.label: extractTokenCode
nodes.rationale: Accepts either a bare code or a status-page URL, so one scanner handles both printed codes and QR links without the staff choosing a mode.

nodes.label: normalizePhone (E.164)
nodes.rationale: Bare 10-digit numbers get the configured default country code, so devotees can enter a local number while Twilio still receives E.164.

nodes.label: isObjectId
nodes.rationale: Adds a 24-character length check on top of mongoose.isValidObjectId, which otherwise accepts any 12-byte string.

nodes.label: zonedParts (Intl part extraction)
nodes.rationale: Formatters are memoized per timezone because Intl.DateTimeFormat construction is expensive and slot generation calls it thousands of times.

nodes.label: zonedTimeToUtc
nodes.rationale: Two-pass offset resolution: the first guess is corrected once if the resulting instant falls under a different UTC offset, so local HH:mm maps correctly across DST transitions without a date library.

nodes.label: localDateStr
nodes.rationale: Dates travel through the system as 'YYYY-MM-DD' strings in the temple's own calendar, so slot days are correct regardless of the server's timezone.

nodes.label: End-to-end API test suite
nodes.rationale: Runs against a live stack over HTTP rather than mocking the services, so the seeded database, sockets, ML service and Twilio mock are all exercised as one system; assertions are printed PASS/FAIL with a failure counter instead of using a test framework.

nodes.label: Gate scan rejection scenarios
nodes.rationale: Asserts on the machine-readable error codes (TOO_EARLY, NOT_ENTERED, ALREADY_ENTERED, ENTRY_PAUSED) rather than message text, so wording can change without breaking the suite.

nodes.label: Forecast source assertion
nodes.rationale: Requires source === 'ml-model', so the test fails loudly if the Python service is down and the historical-average fallback silently takes over.

nodes.label: Temple scoping / RBAC scenarios
nodes.rationale: Explicitly checks that an admin cannot escape their own temple via the X-Temple-Id header while a superadmin must supply it, pinning down the scoping rule in both directions.

nodes.label: Smart Darshan System
nodes.rationale: Devotees wait hours because crowds are unplanned and the queue is invisible; the system spreads arrivals across bookable slots, counts people at gates via QR, publishes live waiting times and predicts crowds hourly.

nodes.label: Python Flask Prediction Service
nodes.rationale: Kept as a separate Flask process so Python ML tooling can be used without pulling scikit-learn into the Node runtime; the API degrades gracefully when it is unreachable.

nodes.label: MongoDB Data Store
nodes.rationale: Local binary downloaded for development so contributors need nothing installed; MongoDB Atlas via MONGO_URI for deployment.

nodes.label: Token Lifecycle State Machine
nodes.rationale: booked -> checked_in (entry scan) -> completed (exit scan), plus cancelled and expired when the slot is missed; devotees still in the queue after 3 hours are completed automatically so the queue count cannot drift upward from missed exit scans.

nodes.label: Automatic Slot Generation
nodes.rationale: Slots are pre-generated for a 7-day booking window so capacity is bounded in advance and arrivals are spread instead of clustering.

nodes.label: Darshan Type (Sarva, Special Entry, Senior Citizen)
nodes.rationale: Each type carries its own slot length, capacity and queue lane, so lanes can be measured and predicted independently.
nodes.norm_label: darshan type (sarva, special entry, senior citizen)

nodes.label: Festival Capacity Multiplier
nodes.rationale: Festival days get extra capacity (default 1.5x) because demand predictably spikes and fixed capacity would push everyone into walk-in queues.

nodes.label: Online / Walk-in Quota Split
nodes.rationale: Every slot's capacity is split (e.g. 50/50) so devotees who cannot book online are never crowded out by online bookings.

nodes.label: Walk-in Seat Release Rule
nodes.rationale: Within 60 minutes of a slot starting, unsold online seats become available to walk-ins, so reserved-but-unused capacity is not wasted while walk-ins queue.

nodes.label: Atomic Seat Reservation (No Overbooking)
nodes.rationale: Capacity check and seat increment happen in one Slot.findOneAndUpdate with an $expr guard and $inc, so two devotees racing for the last seats can never both succeed; a read-then-write check would leave a race window.

nodes.label: Kiosk and Counter Access Channel
nodes.rationale: Devotees without smartphones get printed tokens at the counter or a self-service kiosk, keeping one token system for everyone.

nodes.label: Gate QR Scan as Crowd Sensor
nodes.rationale: The entry/exit QR scan is the only 'sensor' in the system - no hardware counters or cameras are needed, so the deployment stays software-only.
nodes.norm_label: gate qr scan as crowd sensor

nodes.label: Wait-Time Engine (inQueue / throughput)
nodes.rationale: waitMin = inQueue / throughput, where inQueue counts people scanned in and not yet out and throughput is exits in the last 15 minutes per minute observed; the lane's designed capacity is used as throughput until enough real exits are observed, avoiding divide-by-zero and wild early estimates.

nodes.label: Queue Position Calculation
nodes.rationale: A devotee's position counts people who entered the same lane before them, so position is lane-scoped rather than temple-wide.

nodes.label: Crowd Control Alerts and Entry Pause
nodes.rationale: Alerts fire at 90% and 100% of the temple's safe limit; admins pause entry with a reason that gate scanners enforce and devotees see instantly, with optional automatic pause at 100%.
nodes.norm_label: crowd control alerts and entry pause

nodes.label: Hourly Footfall Log
nodes.rationale: Each scan rolls up into an hourly record (temple, date, hour, weekday, festival flag, entries) - the aggregate is what the model needs, and it keeps training data small.

nodes.label: Cyclic Time Feature Set
nodes.rationale: Hour, day of week, month, weekend flag, festival flag, plus hour encoded cyclically as sin/cos so that hour 23 and hour 0 are adjacent in feature space.

nodes.label: Per-Temple Random Forest Regressor
nodes.rationale: RandomForestRegressor with 200 trees, one model per temple because crowd rhythms differ by temple; evaluated on a 20% test split.

nodes.label: Weekday-Hour Average Baseline
nodes.rationale: The service reports R2 and MAE alongside the MAE of a naive 'average for this weekday and hour' baseline, so the model's improvement is demonstrable rather than asserted.

nodes.label: Hourly Crowd Forecast Output
nodes.rationale: Expected visitors per hour, a crowd level (low/moderate/high against capacity), the peak hour and the 3 least crowded hours - the least-crowded hours turn a prediction into an actionable booking suggestion.

nodes.label: Model Retraining Schedule
nodes.rationale: Trains at API startup for untrained temples, after seeding, nightly at 02:30, or on demand from the Analytics page Retrain button.

nodes.label: Historical-Average Forecast Fallback
nodes.rationale: If the Python service is down, forecasts fall back to historical averages so the whole app keeps working rather than failing on an optional feature.

nodes.label: SMS Mock Console Mode
nodes.rationale: Without Twilio credentials messages print to the API console as [sms:mock], so development needs no paid account or real phone numbers.

nodes.label: Inbound SMS Command Set (STATUS / WAIT / TEMPLES)
nodes.rationale: A Twilio messaging webhook at POST /api/sms/inbound gives basic-phone users queue position, live wait times and the temple list without any app; testable with plain curl.
nodes.norm_label: inbound sms command set (status / wait / temples)

nodes.label: In-App Real-Time Notifications
nodes.rationale: Booking confirmations, queue entry, 30-minute slot reminders and expiry notices arrive over Socket.IO as toasts, plus browser notifications when enabled.

nodes.label: Socket.IO Rooms and Event Channels
nodes.rationale: Clients subscribe with {type: temple|token|admin, id}; the server emits live:update, slot:update, token:update, announcement:new, alert:new and notification (to the logged-in user's room), so each viewer receives only relevant pushes.

nodes.label: Entrance Display Board
nodes.rationale: A public screen at the entrance serves devotees with no phone at all, reusing the same live snapshot as dashboards and devotee phones.

nodes.label: Four-Role Access Model
nodes.rationale: devotee, staff, admin and superadmin, so gate scanning, temple administration and multi-temple onboarding are separable duties.

nodes.label: Temple Scope Enforcement Middleware
nodes.rationale: Staff and admins are locked to their own temple on the server and the temple id is never taken from the URL, so a tampered path cannot reach another temple's data; only a superadmin selects a temple, via the X-Temple-Id header.

nodes.label: JWT Bearer Authentication
nodes.rationale: Passwords hashed with bcrypt, sessions carried as Authorization: Bearer JWTs; login and register are rate-limited and helmet sets security headers.

nodes.label: Public Token Page Privacy Masking
nodes.rationale: The public token page masks the devotee's name and never shows the phone number; the token code itself acts as the secret, so a shareable status link leaks no personal data.

nodes.label: Scheduled Cron Jobs
nodes.rationale: Expire tokens, send reminders, sync slots and retrain models on a schedule so state stays correct without user action.

nodes.label: Seed and Gate Simulation Scripts
nodes.rationale: Seeding creates 3 temples and 90 days of realistic history (morning/evening peaks, weekend and festival surges) so the ML model has something to learn; simulate drives walk-ins and entry/exit scans so live behaviour is demonstrable without a real crowd.

nodes.label: Brand Typography and Theme Color
nodes.rationale: Inter for UI text and Marcellus as a display face, with theme-color #7c2d12, giving the app a temple-appropriate identity; fonts are preconnected to reduce first-paint delay.

nodes.label: Rationale: Flat Geometric Temple Mark Legible at 16px
nodes.norm_label: rationale: flat geometric temple mark legible at 16px

nodes.label: Token Status Lifecycle (booked -> checked_in -> completed / cancelled / expired)
nodes.rationale: TOKEN_STATUSES enumerates the five states and each transition writes its own timestamp field (checkedInAt, completedAt, cancelledAt, expiredAt) instead of a status-history array, so queue queries can filter and sort on a single indexed date. `autoCompleted` distinguishes a sweeper-completed token from a staff-completed one.
nodes.norm_label: token status lifecycle (booked -> checked_in -> completed / cancelled / expired)

nodes.label: ACTIVE_STATUSES (seat-consuming states)
nodes.rationale: booked + checked_in + completed count against slot capacity; only cancelled and expired release seats, which is what makes cancellation a capacity-returning operation.

nodes.label: Denormalized Slot Fields on Token
nodes.rationale: slotDate, slotStartAt, slotEndAt and darshanTypeName are copied from the slot at booking time, explicitly commented as 'so queue and reminder queries need no join'. Trade-off accepted: stale copies if a slot is rescheduled, in exchange for single-collection live queue reads.

nodes.label: Token Compound Index Strategy
nodes.rationale: Five compound indexes, each shaped for one read path: temple+status+darshanType+checkedInAt for the live lane queue, temple+completedAt for throughput stats, temple+slotDate for day views, userId+slotStartAt desc for 'my tokens', status+slotStartAt for the global expiry sweeper.

nodes.label: Token Actor Audit Fields (issuedBy / checkedInBy / completedBy)
nodes.rationale: Each staff-driven lifecycle transition records which user performed it, giving a per-token audit trail without a separate log collection.
nodes.norm_label: token actor audit fields (issuedby / checkedinby / completedby)

nodes.label: findTokenByCode (code lookup helper)
nodes.rationale: Runs the raw path param through extractTokenCode so a pasted QR URL, a lowercase code or an SMS body all resolve to the same canonical SD-XXXXXX code before the DB hit; an unparseable code short-circuits to the same 404 as a missing one, leaking nothing.

nodes.label: canSeeFullToken (visibility predicate)
nodes.rationale: Full detail is granted to the owning devotee, any superadmin, or staff/admin whose templeId matches the token's temple; everyone else (including anonymous scanners of a found ticket) gets the masked projection.

nodes.label: myTokens handler (scoped booking list)
nodes.rationale: Partitions the lifecycle into upcoming (booked, checked_in) and past (completed, cancelled, expired), flips the slotStartAt sort direction per scope, caps at 100, then batch-loads the referenced temples into a Map to avoid an N+1 populate. Tokens whose temple is missing are dropped rather than rendered half-empty.

nodes.label: getTokenStatus handler (public status endpoint)
nodes.rationale: Returns token + live queue + isOwner in one payload so the status page can render ticket, queue panel and the cancel affordance from a single request that works signed-in or anonymous.

nodes.label: serializeToken (token API DTO)
nodes.rationale: Single shaping function for every token response, so the public status page, my-tokens list and staff screens all consume one contract. It embeds resolved temple and darshanType objects (including isPriority looked up from the temple subdocument) so clients never need a second fetch, and it is the only place the full-vs-masked decision is applied.

nodes.label: Entry Window Computation (opensAt / closesAt)
nodes.rationale: Derived server-side from slotStartAt minus temple settings.checkinEarlyMin and slotEndAt plus checkinLateMin, so the grace period is a per-temple setting and every client prints identical gate times without knowing the rule.

nodes.label: canCancel Derived Flag
nodes.rationale: Computed as status === 'booked' AND slot start still in the future; shipping it as a boolean keeps the cancellation rule server-authoritative while letting the UI hide the button.

nodes.label: Devotee Name Masking Policy (full vs masked projection)
nodes.rationale: A token code is a bearer identifier printed on paper, so the public projection masks the devotee name and omits the phone entirely; anyone who scans a dropped ticket sees queue position but not a contactable identity.
nodes.norm_label: devotee name masking policy (full vs masked projection)

nodes.label: Token Router (/tokens)
nodes.rationale: Booking is restricted to the devotee role and validated with zod (slotId, groupSize, name, phone); the listing and cancel routes require auth, while status alone is open.

nodes.label: GET /tokens/:code (optionalAuth public status route)
nodes.rationale: optionalAuth rather than authenticate: the QR must resolve for a phone camera with no session, yet an authenticated owner or staff member on the same URL gets the full projection.

nodes.label: TokenTicket (devotee darshan ticket)
nodes.rationale: Documented intent: the QR encodes the public status URL so a phone camera opens live status while the gate scanner reads the token code out of the same image - one artifact serves devotee and staff. Terminal statuses dim the QR to 40% opacity as a visual dead-token cue, and the entry-window hint renders only while status is 'booked'.

nodes.label: tokenUrl (QR payload builder)
nodes.rationale: Builds origin + /t/<code> so the QR is a plain scannable https URL rather than an opaque payload, making the ticket work with any stock camera app and keeping the code recoverable from the URL by the server's extractTokenCode.

nodes.label: TokenSlip (printable walk-in slip)
nodes.rationale: Narrow print-area layout for a counter printer or kiosk: oversized monospace code so it is readable and dictatable without a phone, plus the same QR payload as the on-screen ticket and an SMS fallback line for devotees with feature phones.

nodes.label: MyTokens page (devotee booking list)
nodes.rationale: Promotes the first upcoming token to a full TokenTicket with a 'next visit' call-to-action and renders the remainder as compact rows, so the ticket a devotee is about to use is the one showing its QR. Reloads on any socket 'notification' event.

nodes.label: Upcoming / Past Scope Filter
nodes.rationale: The client sends only an opaque scope word; the mapping from scope to lifecycle statuses lives on the server, so the status partition cannot drift between tiers.

nodes.label: TokenStatus page (/t/:code live status)
nodes.rationale: The QR destination: renders ticket plus live queue for owner and anonymous scanner alike from one endpoint, with print styling (print-area / no-print) so the same page doubles as the printable ticket.

nodes.label: QueuePanel (queue state renderer)
nodes.rationale: Branches on the server-computed queue.state rather than on token.status directly - in_queue shows position/people-ahead/ETA, upcoming and entry_open show the entry window and current lane wait, and the terminal branch maps completed/cancelled/expired to icon, tone and copy. Defaulting an unknown state to 'completed' means a new state would silently render as a success screen.

nodes.label: Cancel Booking Flow (confirm modal)
nodes.rationale: Gated on isOwner AND the server's canCancel flag, then a modal that names the seat count being released - the confirmation copy frames cancellation as returning capacity to other devotees.

nodes.label: Live Status Update Strategy (socket rooms + throttle + poll)
nodes.rationale: Three layered triggers: join the token room and reload on token:update (this devotee's own transition), join the temple room and reload on live:update throttled to 4s (lane-wide movement, which is high frequency), and a 60s interval as a floor if the socket drops.
nodes.norm_label: live status update strategy (socket rooms + throttle + poll)

nodes.label: SMS "STATUS <code>" Fallback Channel
nodes.rationale: Both the printed slip and the web status page advertise the same SMS keyword, so a devotee with no smartphone gets the same queue information keyed by the same token code.

nodes.label: TrackToken page (manual code entry)
nodes.rationale: Non-QR entry point for devotees whose camera fails or who were read the code aloud; it only navigates, leaving all lookup and error handling to the status page.

nodes.label: Client Token Code Normalization (SD- prefix, uppercase)
nodes.rationale: Trims, uppercases and re-adds the SD- prefix when the devotee types only the suffix, so the fragment people actually read off a slip resolves to a valid URL.
nodes.norm_label: client token code normalization (sd- prefix, uppercase)
